description: Verdicts are assigned mechanically from two order-swapped judgements,
not chosen by the judge: the judge only picks a winner each time.
A verdict is directional only when both orderings agree, which is what
makes 'inconsistent' mean 'indistinguishable to this judge' rather than
The unit is a COMPARISON — one test question against one transition —
not a transition. Three models were sampled with two questions per
transition, so 76 comparisons cover 58 distinct transitions.

verdicts.B_better: The committed successor L_(n+1) won in both presentation orders.
verdicts.A_better: The parent L_n won in both presentation orders.
verdicts.inconsistent: The winner flipped with presentation order — indistinguishable.
verdicts.parse_error: The judge did not return parseable JSON in one of the orders.

judges.L0: the bare model, no system prompt
